_about: Everything villagers say (all drafts for Alex). 'gift_lines' are what they say to a gift they don't love (by villager, then item); anything missing gets a polite thank-you. {sweater} = Rosa's sweater price today, {cottage} = cottage price, {rent} = cottage rent. 'lines' has three tiers per villager: 0-1 hearts, 2-3 hearts, 4-5 hearts.

intro.rosa: Oh, a new face! I'm Rosa. The Yarn Barn's mine, and some mornings you'll find me on the market stall instead. Wool, yarn, the odd sheep, and I buy sweaters: {sweater}c each today.
intro.gary: Gary. Willow Homes. Property, prospects, and frankly the best hair in the valley. You're Ellie's granddaughter? Lovely. Starter farm. We all start somewhere.
intro.giorgio: Come in, come in, out of the cold. Giorgio. Everything in that case I made before the sun was up. Sit down. You look like someone who forgot to eat.
intro.sabrina: Hi. Welcome to the Coffee Shop. Yes, that's the actual name. No, I didn't pick it. What do you want?
intro.steve: Steve. Builder's Delight. Wood, nails, hinges. Ask.
intro.rowan: Rowan. I keep the flock on the hill past your place. If you hear bleating at dawn, that's mine. Probably.
intro.wren: Wren. Mayor. Sorry, I've got four minutes. If something's broken, tell me. If it's on fire, tell me faster.
intro.barbara: Hello, sweetheart. Barbara, with the post. Nine o'clock, every door, rain or shine. Yours too, now. That's how you know you live somewhere.

rosa: Sweaters are going for {sweater}c today. Prices change every morning, so check the board.
Out of wool? Three bundles makes one sweater, if you don't drop stitches.
If you ever grow pumpkins, save one for me. I make a mean pie.
You're becoming my favourite supplier! I pay you a little extra now: {sweater}c a sweater today.
I put one of your sweaters in the Yarn Barn window. Three people asked who made it!
Stall in the morning, shop in the afternoon. My feet hate me. My till loves me.
Between us, I tell customers your sweaters are 'Birchfield originals.' They pay more for the name!
My late husband would have loved your farm. He always said the best things are made slowly.
You've got a real knitting empire going, love. {sweater}c a sweater, just for you.
gary: Real estate is simple: location, location, and me.
Every piece of furniture in a rental raises the rent. People pay for cozy. I pay for nothing. That's the trick.
Your farm has character. That's what we say when a place has damp.
You've got a good eye. Not as good as mine, but nobody's perfect. Well. One of us is.
Eastfield Acres is still on the market. It won't be forever. It will be for a while, at that price.
I take a little off for friends. Don't tell anyone we're friends. Bad for my image.
You're my favourite client. I say that to everyone, but this time I nearly mean it.
One day you'll own half this valley, and I'll have sold you every acre of it.
Keep this up and they'll name a street after you. I'll handle the sale of the street.
giorgio: Cold butter, warm kitchen, up at four. That's the whole secret. Mostly the up-at-four part.
Eat first. Whatever it is, it looks smaller after a croissant.
I came here for the quiet. The quiet stayed. So did I.
I've started saving you the corner pieces. Don't tell anyone or they'll all want corners.
You flinch when the oven door bangs. I know that flinch. You don't have to explain it to me.
Your gran liked her loaf dark. 'Burn it a little, Giorgio.' I still bake one her way on Sundays.
Some people run to something. Some people run from something. The bread doesn't care which. Neither do I.
If you want to learn the croissants, come by at four. I'll have the kettle on.
You're doing well, cara. Better than you think. I'd tell you if you weren't.
sabrina: If you're going to stand there, at least order something.
No, we don't do oat milk. We do milk. From a cow. Welcome to Maple Grove.
My manager says I have to smile at customers. This is me smiling.
You're here a lot. It's fine. It's not weird. It's a little weird.
I made a heart in your foam. It's a blob. Don't read into it.
Okay, fine, your sweater's actually kind of cool. Don't tell anyone I said cool.
I'm saving for art school. Don't laugh. ...You didn't laugh. Okay. Thanks.
You're like the only person here who doesn't treat me like a kid. Just so you know.
I saved you the last cinnamon roll. I fought a man for it. Not really. Kind of.
steve: Your gran's broom. Bought it here. Every five years.
Got a nice bit of oak out back. Not for sale. Just like looking at it.
Hm. Good hinge, that. You'll be fine.
You build like your gran knitted. Bit crooked. All heart.
Kettle's on in the back. If you want. No pressure.
Anyone gives you trouble, you tell me. ...That's all.
rowan: Your fence on the east side leans. I'd fix it before the ewes notice.
Weather's turning. Sheep always know first.
Most folks who move out here from the city last a season. You've got a look like you might stay.
You've got wool on your sleeve. Suits you.
I walked past your place last night. Light was on late. Knitting, or not sleeping?
Rosa won't stop talking about your work. Takes a lot to get Rosa talking. Well. Less than you'd think.
I used to hate quiet evenings. Lately I don't mind them.
If you ever want to see the hill at sunset, I know the best rock to sit on.
You don't have to tell me what you left behind. But I'd listen, if you wanted.
wren: Fountain's leaking. It's on the list. Everything's on the list.
Can't stop. Meeting. Probably about the bench.
Your gran ran the harvest fair. Nobody's dared take it over. Not my problem today.
You're settling in. Good. One less thing.
Sorry. Bad week. It's always a bad week. Don't ask.
If you need a hand at the farm, say so. Quickly. I'm due somewhere.
You're good for this town. I don't say that. I'm saying it. Okay, I have to go.
Some mornings I walk past your farm just to see the chimney smoke. Then I'm late. Worth it.
There's something I've been meaning to tell someone. Not today. Soon, maybe.
barbara: Nothing in the bag for you today, sweetheart. No news is often the kindest news.
Walk slowly in a new town. You'll see more, and you'll be seen.
Rain or shine, the post gets through. Mostly shine round here, thank goodness.
Your gran left a biscuit on the gatepost for me every morning. I'm only mentioning it.
The letters you dread are never as heavy as the waiting for them.
You don't have to be brave every day. Some days you just have to open the door.
If a letter comes for you from the city, I'll bring it to your hand myself. Not leave it in the box.
Best part of my round is the bit past your farm. It smells like hay and woodsmoke, and hope.
Forty years I've carried other people's news. Yours is turning into a good story.

rosa.sweater: For me? Oh, you'll make me cry in front of customers and then nobody buys anything.
rosa.turnip: A good firm turnip. You know the way to a market woman's heart: produce.

gary.pumpkin: A pumpkin. I'll put it on the office step. Makes the place look settled. Buyers love settled.
gary.turnip: A turnip. For me. ...I'll give it to someone who knows what to do with one.

giorgio.turnip: A turnip! That's soup. Thank you, cara. It'll be on the counter by lunch.
giorgio.sweater: For me? It's so soft. I'm keeping it well away from the flour.

sabrina.pumpkin: It's a pumpkin. Cool. I'll put it on the counter. It's... actually kind of cute there.
sabrina.turnip: Why would you give a person a turnip.

steve.sweater: ...Warm. Thank you. I'll wear it Sundays.

rowan.pumpkin: Soup, then. I'll make it badly and eat it anyway. Thanks.
rowan.turnip: A turnip. ... The ewes will think I've gone soft. Thank you.

barbara.pumpkin: Oh, a pumpkin! That's a pie for the sorting room. Bless you.
barbara.sweater: You made this? I'll wear it on my round and tell every door it's yours.

gift_loved.rosa: A pumpkin! Oh, you remembered. I'm baking a pie tonight and you're getting the first slice.
gift_loved.gary: Is this one of YOUR sweaters? I'll wear it to viewings. Hand-knit, local, authentic. I'll triple my sales.
gift_loved.giorgio: Pumpkin! Bread, soup, a tart for the window... Come back tomorrow, there'll be something in it for you.
gift_loved.sabrina: Wait, you made this? For me? ...Okay. It's really nice. Like, really nice. Don't look at me.
gift_loved.steve: Now that's a pumpkin. Going on the counter. Best-looking thing in the shop.
gift_loved.rowan: You made this. For me. ... I don't really know what to say. Thank you. I'll wear it up on the hill.
gift_loved.wren: For me? Oh. Oh, this is beautiful. I haven't got time to cry. I'm going to anyway.
gift_loved.barbara: A turnip! You remembered. Nobody remembers. That's going in tonight's stew, sweetheart.
